requests.transportRule: literal parameterless route; the handler reads no route value, no query string and no body and constructs new GetShippingAuthoringContextQuery() with zero arguments
requests.reason: Effective edition, default currency and content languages are resolved server-side from trusted context and Contracts; there is no caller-controlled transport input, so a validator would own nothing. The classification is proven by the guard, not asserted from intent.

requests.transportRule: literal parameterless routes; each handler constructs the request from a server-built ShippingAuthoringOwnerScope and reads no route value, no query string and no body
requests.reason: The owner scope is resolved and authorized by the server on every request; there is no caller-controlled transport input, so a validator would own nothing. The classification is proven by the guard, not asserted from intent.

requests.transportRule: service code non-empty/bounded, option code bounded, region group tree shape coherent (kind matches deepest id), group/selection counts within technical payload bounds; the owner is never part of the body
requests.reason: A full draft tree is submitted by the caller, so every untrusted id, level and count must be rejected with a stable code before any method/geography/business validation runs.

requests.transportRule: draftId non-empty, expectedRevision positive integer, region group tree shape coherent within technical payload bounds; owner/tenant/seller are never bound from transport
requests.reason: The replacement replaces a whole tree and carries an optimistic-concurrency token, so both the id and the revision are caller-controlled and must be shape-validated.

requests.transportRule: literal parameterless routes; the handler builds the request from the server-authorized owner scope and reads no route value, query string or body
requests.reason: There is no caller-controlled transport input on this read; a validator would own nothing, and the owner filter is the authorization result, not a request field.

requests.transportRule: draftId non-empty; a foreign or unknown id returns the same safe not-found response
requests.reason: The draft id comes from the route and is projected into the read request, so its shape is transport-owned even though ownership is decided by the server filter.

requests.transportRule: both route ids non-empty; the group is only ever sought INSIDE the owner-filtered draft, so a foreign or invented id returns the same safe not-found response
requests.reason: Two caller-supplied route ids are projected into the read request; neither ownership nor geography is taken from transport.

requests.transportRule: route ids non-empty, expectedRevision positive, rows collection REQUIRED ([] allowed), retained row ids non-empty and unique, half-open interval coherence and technical bounds per axis, canonical money precision, delivery duration present with min <= max; owner, tenant, seller and currency are never bound from transport
requests.reason: A whole untrusted row collection, its ranges, amounts and the shared optimistic-concurrency token are caller-controlled; the trusted currency is read server-side BEFORE any tracked write.

requests.transportRule: the route draft id must be non-empty; the draft is only ever sought INSIDE the owner-filtered scope, so a foreign or invented id returns the same safe not-found response
requests.reason: One caller-supplied route id is projected into the read request. Content language is never taken from route/query/Accept-Language; stored text and the active registry are returned truthfully.

requests.transportRule: route draft id non-empty, expectedRevision positive, both collections REQUIRED ([] is a valid no-op), no null entries, language ids non-empty and unique per item, (group,language) pairs unique, name non-blank and bounded, description/title bounded; owner, mode, tenant, currency and active-language facts are never bound from transport
requests.reason: Two whole untrusted language-keyed collections and the shared optimistic-concurrency token are caller-controlled; the active language set is resolved from the TB-188 authoritative source BEFORE any tracked write and invalid/inactive ids fail closed.

requests.transportRule: the route draft id must be non-empty; the draft is only ever sought INSIDE the owner-filtered scope, so a foreign or invented id returns the same safe not-found response
requests.reason: One caller-supplied route id is projected into the read request. Absence of a schedule is reported truthfully as UNCONFIGURED; no timezone, hour or seven-day default is fabricated for the reader.

requests.transportRule: route draft id non-empty, expectedRevision positive, timezone non-blank and bounded, the days collection REQUIRED and exactly seven entries with no null element, an explicitly present working flag per day, paired local times with end > start; owner, tenant, seller, mode, currency, language and geography are never bound from transport and timezone resolvability/exactly-seven uniqueness stay canonical domain preflight rules
requests.reason: A whole untrusted week and the shared optimistic-concurrency token are caller-controlled; a missing working flag must never deserialize into an implicit closed day, and an omitted/duplicated weekday is a shape failure before any tracked write.

amendments.scope: One additive authorized GET (admin authoring context) is classified here. No previous row changed classification, validator, route or handler.
amendments.noValidatorProvenance: GetShippingAuthoringContextQuery is constructed with zero arguments in a literal, parameterless route; the endpoint binds no route value, no query string and no body, so there is no caller-controlled transport input for a validator to own. The guard proves absence (no IValidator<T>, no route template parameters, no request Query/body access in the handler body) instead of trusting the label.

amendments.scope: Two additive authorized GETs (admin and seller authoring owner) share ONE request. The row is therefore keyed by request and carries both route provenance paths; one route is not assumed to equal one request, and no route is left unclassified.
amendments.sharedRequestProvenance: GetShippingAuthoringOwnerQuery is constructed exactly once per route in the endpoint delegate, from a ShippingAuthoringOwnerScope built by executed server authorization (admin trusted installation gate, or seller panel gate + effective whole-owner permission). No route value, query string or body is bound and no owner/mode/tenant/seller field is forwarded from transport, so a validator would own nothing.

amendments.scope: Two additive authorized requests (GET/PUT group rate rows) are classified here, each reachable through one admin and one seller route. No previous row changed classification, validator, route or handler.
amendments.currencyProvenance: The replace command binds NO currency from transport. The trusted default currency is read from IShippingAuthoringContextSource (TB-188 Contracts-only seam over StoreContext) BEFORE any tracked write; an unresolved edition/currency fails closed with shipping.authoring.configuration_unavailable. The stored group currency is returned truthfully on read and a mismatch is refused rather than reinterpreted.

amendments.scope: Two additive authorized requests (GET/PUT owner weekly operating schedule) are classified here, each reachable through one admin and one seller route. No previous row changed classification, validator, route or handler.
amendments.scheduleProvenance: The schedule is attached ONCE to the draft/method and shared by all its region groups. The body carries NO owner, tenant, seller, mode, geography, currency, language or per-group field. The explicit timezone is validated by the canonical ShippingScheduleRules.NormalizeTimeZone (extracted from the legacy schedule aggregate with identical codes/behavior); resolvability is a domain preflight rule, not a foreign timezone catalog. Absent schedule = UNCONFIGURED, never seven implicit working days; an all-closed week is seven real rows and is distinct.
